gen-dafont-junegull-gf-puritan: Friendly and a bit retro, Junegull draws its lowercase tall and sturdy like cast iron capitals. Puritan follows in a plain sans, rounded and wide-countered, so a longer passage goes down smoothly.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-questrial: Junegull has a retro, friendly pinch at the mouth of every curve, closing its letters up tight. Questrial goes the other way, flat and open in single-weight strokes, so a longer passage reads crisp and modern.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-radio-canada:
Radio Canada keeps its curves open and full.

Junegull pinches its curves shut, and that closed-versus-open split between the two is the pair's strongest quality, with the sans below standing tall and steady.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-readex-pro: Retro swagger up top, quiet order below, with Junegull's pinched curves set over a sans of broad terminal gaps. The open-versus-closed split is the draw.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-roboto:
Retro and cheerful, with a pen-nib look.

Junegull is best at pinched, cast-iron-tall display letters, while Roboto, a sans-serif with generous round mouths and little height difference between capitals and lowercase, handles the running text.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-ruda:
Ruda is a wiry monoline sans-serif.

Junegull's closed, pinched curves sit above its wide-mouthed rounds and sizable x-height, so the heading feels tight and the text beneath it breathes freely.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-saira:
Saira lets you see right through each s, with rounded letters stretching high toward the top line.

Against Junegull's thread-thin ink, a longer passage feels smooth.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-sarpanch: Junegull's line has the steady, unswelling feel of a technical drafting pen, with retro charm in its pinched curves. And Sarpanch, a sans-serif with a clearly open e, makes the pair's strongest quality its tight-versus-open contrast.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-schibsted-grotesk: Junegull draws spaghetti-like strokes of one width, with retro, friendly pinched curves. Schibsted Grotesk, a plain sans with big open e and a shapes and terminals that never close in, makes a longer passage feel easygoing.
gen-dafont-junegull-gf-sen: Junegull is retro and friendly, with a tall lowercase and curves pinched nearly shut. Sen, a plain sans built tall in constant-weight lines that stop before turning inward, probably wants a size slightly above the usual.
